faces.f: Benalia has a complex caste system that changes with the lunar year. No matter what the season, the only caste that cannot be attained by either heredity or money is that of the hero.

Before a woman marries in the village of Sursi, she must visit the land of the Mesa Pegasus. Legend has it that if the woman is pure of heart and her love is true, a Mesa Pegasus will appear, blessing her family with long life and good fortune.

"Look to the north; there you will find aid and comfort."
—The Book of Tal

"'Do you know, I always thought Unicorns were fabulous monsters, too? I never saw one alive before!' 'Well, now that we have seen each other,' said the Unicorn, 'if you'll believe in me, I'll believe in you.'" —Lewis Carroll
Healers ultimately acquire the divine gifts of spiritual and physical wholeness. The most devout are also granted the ability to pass physical wholeness on to others.

The traditional kings of the jungle command a healthy respect in other climates as well. Relying mainly on their stealth and speed, Savannah Lions can take a victim by surprise, even in the endless flat plains of their homeland.
Born with wings of light and a sword of faith, this heavenly incarnation embodies both fury and purity.
Good bodyguards are hard to find, mainly because they don't live long.

Just as the evil ones approached to slay Justina, she cast a great spell, imbuing her weapons with her own life force. Thus she fulfilled the prophecy: "In the death of your savior will you find salvation."
Out of the blackness and stench of the engulfing swamp emerged a shimmering figure. Only the splattered armor and ichor-stained sword hinted at the unfathomable evil the knight had just laid waste.
These spirits of the air are winsome and wild, and cannot be truly contained. Only marginally intelligent, they often substitute whimsy for strategy, delighting in mischief and mayhem.
A master of tactics, the Lord of Atlantis makes his people bold in battle merely by arriving to lead them.
Of royal blood among the spirits of the air, the Mahamoti Djinn rides on the wings of the winds. As dangerous in the gambling hall as he is in battle, he is a master of trickery and misdirection.

Most human scholars believe that Merfolk are the survivors of sunken Atlantis, humans adapted to the water. Merfolk, however, believe that humans sprang forth from Merfolk who adapted themselves in order to explore their last frontier.
These beings embody the essence of true heroes long dead. Summoned from the dreamrealms, they rise to meet their enemies.

"While, like a ghastly rapid river,
Through the pale door,
A hideous throng rush out forever,
And laugh—but smile no more."
—Edgar Allan Poe, "The Haunted Palace"
Occasionally a member of the Institute of Arcane Study acquires a taste for worldly pleasures. Seldom do they have trouble finding employment.
Legend has it that Serpents used to be bigger, but how could that be?
"This 'standing windstorm' can hold us off indefinitely? Ridiculous!" Saying nothing, she put a pinch of salt on the table. With a bang she clapped her hands, and the salt disappeared, blown away.
A deafening roar arose as the fury of an enormous vertical river supplanted our serenity. Eddies turned into whirling geysers, leveling everything in their path.

Unpredictable as the sea itself, Water Elementals shift without warning from tranquility to tempest. Capricious and fickle, they flow restlessly from one shape to another, expressing their moods with their physical forms.
Battle doesn't need a purpose; the battle is its own purpose. You don't ask why a plague spreads or a field burns. Don't ask why I fight.
'Twas in the bogs of Cannelbrae My mate did meet an early grave 'Twas nothing left for us to save In the peat-filled bogs of Cannelbrae.
Created to destroy Dominia, Demons can sometimes be bent to a more focused purpose.
Bones scattered around us joined to form misshapen bodies. We struck at them repeatedly—they fell, but soon formed again, with the same mocking look on their faceless skulls.

"There are some qualities—some incorporate things,/ That have a double life, which thus is made/ A type of twin entity which springs/ From matter and light, evinced in solid and shade."
—Edgar Allan Poe, "Silence"

"...There was no trace/ Of aught on that illumined face..."
—Samuel Coleridge, "Phantom"
The Nightmare arises from its lair in the swamps. As the poisoned land spreads, so does the Nightmare's rage and terrifying strength.

"Should you a Rat to madness tease
Why ev'n a Rat may plague you..."
—Samuel Coleridge, "Recantation"
Trained in the arts of stealth, the royal assassins choose their victims carefully, relying on timing and precision rather than brute force.

"They groaned, they stirred, they all uprose,/ Nor spake, nor moved their eyes;/ It had been strange, even in a dream,/ To have seen those dead men rise."/ —Samuel Coleridge, "The Rime of the Ancient Mariner"
The Wall of Bone is said to be an aspect of the Great Wall in Hel, where the bones of all sinners wait for Ragnarok, when Hela will call them forth for the final battle.

"About, about in reel and rout
The death-fires danced at night;
The water, like a witch's oils,
Burnt green, and blue and white."
—Samuel Coleridge, "The Rime of the Ancient Mariner"
They say the Zombie Master controlled these foul creatures even before his own death, but now that he is one of them, nothing can make them betray him.

"O to be a dragon . . . of silkworm size or immense . . ."
—Marianne Moore, "O to Be a Dragon"
Foolishly, Najib retreated to his castle at El-Abar; the next morning he was dead. In just one night, the dwarven forces had reduced the mighty walls to mere rubble.

Earth Elementals have the eternal strength of stone and the endurance of mountains. Primordially connected to the land they inhabit, they take a long-term view of things, scorning the impetuous haste of short-lived mortal creatures.

Fire Elementals are ruthless infernos, annihilating and consuming their foes in a frenzied holocaust. Crackling and blazing, they sear swift, terrible paths, leaving the land charred and scorched in their wake.

"And topples round the dreary west
A looming bastion fringed with fire."
—Alfred, Lord Tennyson, "In Memoriam"
"From up here we can drop rocks and arrows and more rocks!" "Uh, yeah boss, but how do we get down?"
To become king of the Goblins, one must assassinate the previous king. Thus, only the most foolish seek positions of leadership.

"While most overworlders fortunately don't realize this, Gargoyles can be most delicious, providing you have the appropriate tools to carve them."
—The Underworld Cookbook, by Asmoranomardicadaistinaculdacar

The Ogre philosopher Gnerdel believed the purpose of life was to live as high on the food chain as possible. She refused to eat vegetarians, and preferred to live entirely on creatures that preyed on sentient beings.
Fortunately, Hill Giants have large blind spots in which a human can easily hide. Unfortunately, these blind spots are beneath the bottoms of their feet.

The Minotaurs of the Hurloon Mountains are known for their love of battle. They are also known for their hymns to the dead, sung for friend and foe alike. These hymns can last for days, filling the mountain valleys with their low, haunting sounds.
Generations of genetic weeding have given rise to the deviously cowardly Ironclaw clan. To say that Orcs in general are vicious, depraved, and ignoble does not do justice to the Ironclaw.

The intricate dynamics of Rundvelt Goblin affairs are often confused with anarchy. The chaos, however, is the chaos of a thundercloud, and direction will sporadically and violently appear. Pashalik Mons and his raiders are the thunderhead that leads in the storm.
In a rare display of ingenuity, the Orcs invented an incredibly destructive weapon. Most Orcish artillerists are those who dared criticize its effectiveness.

We encountered a valley topped with immense boulders and eerie rock formations. Suddenly one of these boulders toppled from its perch and sprouted gargantuan wings, casting a shadow of darkness and sending us fleeing in terror.

The stench in the hovel was overpowering; something loathsome was cooking. Occasionally something surfaced in the thick paste, but my host would casually push it down before I could make out what it was.

While it's true most Dragons are cruel, the Shivan Dragon seems to take particular glee in the misery of others, often tormenting its victims much like a cat plays with a mouse before delivering the final blow.
What goes up, must come down.
None know if this Giant is the result of aberrant magics, Siamese twins, or a mentalist's schizophrenia.

"Oi oi oi, me gotta hurt in 'ere,
Oi oi oi, me smell a ting is near,
Gonna bosh 'n gonna nosh 'n da
hurt'll disappear."
—Traditional
Conjured from the bowels of hell, the fiery wall forms an impassable barrier, searing the soul of any creature attempting to pass through its terrible bursts of flame.

The Earth herself lends her strength to these walls of living stone, which possess the stability of ancient mountains. These mighty bulwarks thwart ground-based troops, providing welcome relief for weary warriors who defend the land.

The most terrifying thing about the Craw Wurm is probably the horrible crashing sound it makes as it speeds through the forest. This noise is so loud it echoes through the trees and seems to come from all directions at once.
I tell you, there was so many arrows flying about you couldn't hardly see the sun. So I says to young Angus, "Well, at least now we're fighting in the shade!"
Rather than sheltering her young, the female Fungusaur often injures her own offspring, thereby ensuring their rapid growth.
While it possesses potent venom, the Giant Spider often chooses not to paralyze its victims. Perhaps the creature enjoys the gentle rocking motion caused by its captives' struggles to escape its web.

Don't try to outrun one of Dominia's Grizzlies; it'll catch you, knock you down, and eat you. Of course, you could run up a tree. In that case you'll get a nice view before it knocks the tree down and eats you.

The mating habits of Treefolk, particularly the stalwart Ironroot Treefolk, are truly absurd. Molasses comes to mind. It's amazing the species can survive at all given such protracted periods of mate selection, conjugation, and gestation.
After years of training, the Druid becomes one with nature, drawing power from the land and returning it when needed.
Whenever the Llanowar Elves gather the fruits of their forest, they leave one plant of each type untouched, considering that nature's portion.
The only sound was the gentle clicking of the Faeries' wings. Then those intruders who were still standing turned and fled. One thing was certain: they didn't think the Scryb were very funny anymore.
Moving without sound, swift figures pass through branches and undergrowth completely unhindered. One with the trees around them, the Dryads of Shanodin Forest are seen only when they wish to be.
Moss-covered statues littered the area, a macabre monument to the Basilisk's power.
Though many think of Wolves as solitary predators, they are actually extremely social animals. During a hunt they often call to each other, which can be quite unsettling for their prey.
Some say magic was first practiced by women, who have always felt strong ties to the land.
"What else, when chaos draws all forces inward to shape a single leaf." —Conrad Aiken

"And through the drifts the snowy cliffs/ Did send a dismal sheen:/ Nor shapes of men nor beasts we ken—/ The ice was all between."/
—Samuel Coleridge, "The Rime of the Ancient Mariner"
Everybody knows that to ward off trouble, you knock on wood. But usually it's better to make a wall out of the wood and let trouble do the knocking.
I didn't think Mammoths could ever hold a candle to a well-trained battle horse. Then one day I turned my back on a drunken soldier. His blow never landed; Mi'cha flung the brute over ten meters.

"Some of the other guys dared me to touch it, but I knew it weren't no ordinary hunk o' rock."
—Norin the Wary
We had taken refuge in a small cave, thinking the entrance was too narrow for it to follow. To our horror, its gigantic head smashed into the mountainside, ripping itself a new entrance.

Some fiendish mage had created a horrifying wall of living flesh, patched together from a jumble of still-recognizable body parts. As we sought to hew our way through it, some unknown power healed the gaping wounds we cut, denying us passage.

"The foot stone is connected to the ankle stone, the ankle stone is connected to the leg stone..."
—Song of the Artificer
The fastest way across the dunes is above.
"Hold the line, for family and the fallen!"
Light streaked down from the heavens, and a voice whispered in the soldier's ear: "You shall not fall today."
"Welcome to the Legion. You saved a district—now let's go save the world."
The angels appreciated the offer but politely declined to eat any birdseed.
He vowed he would never rest until he reached his destination. He doesn't know how right he was.
Its wings disturb more than air.
Honor the gods of Theros, and they will return the favor.
He gasped in wonder even as his body crumbled away.
"Our people are torn by infighting. Until the two sides reconcile, our laws can carry no meaning."
"In these halls there is no pass or fail. Your true test comes with the first full moon."
"Speak little. Do much."
Her resentment vanished as strange, unknown lands opened up before her.
Sometimes gestures of support are small. Sometimes not.

"Your bravery honors us all."
—Dromoka, translated from Draconic
"I don't know where my destiny lies, but I know it isn't here."
With clarity of vision comes clarity of function.
Two taken, two judged, one returned.

"I await your donation."
—Dasha, Orzhov priest

"I search for a vision of Zendikar that does not include the Eldrazi."
—Expedition journal entry
Trust is the only bridle a pegasus will accept.

"Improvement is a consequence of practice."
—Stitcher Geralf
"I am who I pretend to be."
The ideas came flooding in so fast that they couldn't all be contained.
A curse is just another name for an unwanted blessing.
"The specimen seems to be broken."
"Garl, adjust the slurry dispensers. Garl, fetch more corpses. Garl, quit crying and give me your brain tissue. If he doesn't stop being so rude, I'm quitting."
"Try, if you must."
Heads and shoulders above the rest.

"Hop away now, little Eternal. Go eat some flies."
—Kasmina

"It always amazes me what perfectly good things people throw away."
—Ludevic, necro-alchemist
Enthusiasm is no match for preparation.
The fatal flaw in every plan is the assumption that you know more than your enemy.
"The quieter the skies, the calmer the mind."
"My drivers are trustworthy. I removed their tongues myself. Any other questions?"

"I do things in my own time."
—Etha, initiate of Rhet crop

"There's a hole in your plan."
—Noyan Dar, Tazeem lullmage
"The seas are vast, but the skies are even more so. Why be content with one kingdom when I can rule them both?"
He had glimpsed the truth of the Multiverse. Now if only he could remember it.
His marvels of artifice pale in comparison to the developing machinery of his mind.

"It's not the darkness I fear but dull and numbing shades of gray."
—Sydri, galvanic genius
In Lorwyn's brief evenings, the sun pauses at the horizon long enough for a certain species of violet to bloom with the fragrance of mischief.

"Vanya Falkenrath's paintings are astonishing. How does she manage to achieve such rich crimson hues?"
—Stefan, art critic

"Death not for survival but for vanity and pleasure? This is the decadence I sought to curb."
—Sorin Markov

"Later we will mourn those we have lost. First we must end their suffering."
—Drana, Kalastria bloodchief
"Brave scar or unfortunate tale? It all depends on your pain threshold."

"Those without beauty are Lorwyn's greatest tumor. The winnowers have an unpleasant duty, but a necessary one."
—Eidren, perfect of Lys Alana
Having flesh is increasingly a liability on Mirrodin.

"Innistrad's ghoulcallers are talented enough, but let me show you what someone with real power can create."
—Liliana Vess

"Your presence at the palace this evening is required."
—Letter from Queen Marchesa
You will scream out your innermost secrets just to make it stop.

"You have to admit, Gideon—he has great form."
—Liliana Vess

"To death all must go, and so in death lies ultimate power."
—Geth, Lord of the Vault
Deep in Glen Elendra blossoms Oona, queen of the faeries, nourished by secrets and pollinated by stolen dreams.
Dusk follows the light.
"I've seen Ravnica's fate. Believe me, I'm doing you a favor."

"Soul, flesh, even eyes—none of these are strictly necessary for deadly precision."
—Modriss of Zargoth Fen

"Your creations are effective, Sheoldred, but we must unite the flesh, not merely flay it."
—Elesh Norn, Grand Cenobite

"Why limit yourself to mortal law when you can outlive those who enforce it?"
—Czaric, Orzhov prelate

"All are not equal—neither in life nor after death. Bontu's favorites will stand highest in eternity."
—Senifet, vizier of Bontu
All crave the Blessed Sleep. Few receive it.
No matter how deep you bury it, some evil refuses to stay dead.

"Your service shall be rewarded."
—Queen Lian
Scions of the Markov line take particular pleasure in the perversion of humans' holy rituals.
"The time for subtlety is over, darling."
"Greet death with sword in hand."
Hazoret's disappointment at initiates who fail their final trials can manifest in terrible ways.
Memories burn with the brightest flames.
Eyes are unnecessary for seeing the future.
"It's just business."
Magic is the true artist's medium.
Jund feasts on the unprepared.
The Boros banner stands tall even if its bearer doesn't.
Winners of the Iroan Games are forever remembered as heroes of their people.
Viashino thrashes keep iguanars as hunting companions, giving them wounded captives as playthings.
Unhappy with the creation of the wolfir, Rorica broke with her order and led a crusade against the "reformed werewolves."
"It used to be a lair. Now it's just a tunnel."

"Commander, we caught the Dimir spy and took her ashes into custody."
—Kramm, Wojek security officer
The sparkmage shrieked, calling on the rage of the storms of his youth. To his surprise, the sky responded with a fierce energy he'd never thought to see again.
Not all storms come from the sky.
The calligraphy of combat is written with strokes of sudden blood.
Goblins can carry their body weight in loot.

"A touch of lightning, and anyone can be taught to dance."
—Tobin, sparkmage

"She's quick and fearless, and she's never missed a shot. That almost makes up for all the scorch marks she leaves behind."
—Captain Lannery Storm
"One last push, and then my task is done."
"I swear this before all gods old and new: I will fight to my last breath."
Immolation is the sincerest form of flattery.
"Spent a lifetime learning from predators. Picked up a few tricks."
It pairs a long neck with a short temper.

"To survive exceptional times we must adapt by exceptional means."
—Vannifar
Beauty is a seed, waiting to blossom under her capable hands.
Hunters lure the stripling boar into the open, hoping to trap greater prey.

"A herd is only as strong as its weakest. Our weakest just killed his third minotaur raider—today."
—Braulios of Pheres Band
The wolf closed in. But then a strange wind whispered through the leaves, and with a burst of speed, the deer surged forward out of reach.
Even dragons fear its silken strands.
"Mana lurks in all things, even in the depths of one's own heart."
She remembers every word spoken, from the hero's oath to the baby's cry.
Every predator is something else's prey.

"I think it's trying to tell us that the forest is angry."
—Vivien Reid
Emrakul does not grant wishes. Desires simply align to her will.
As the green sun crowned, Phyrexian prophecies glowed on the Tree of Tales.

"Naga shed their scales. We wear ours with pride."
—Golran, dragonscale captain
The ultimate answer to intrigue and subtlety.

"Krosa the great. Krosa the enduring. Look to the forest, and it will share its bounty."
—Zyd, Kamahlite druid
Nature grows solutions to its problems.
Hatred outlives the hateful.
"Aether is the soul of Kaladesh, and all souls should be free."
"All the treasures of this world are grown, not made."
The most successful of Simic creations is cytoplasm, a living, symbiotic substance that feeds off genetic rhythms and strengthens its host in return.
Visiting a shrine at the start of a journey makes the traveler more likely to finish it.
One quiet word sets off the stampede.
Eight legs carrying endless phobias.
Life's circle has become inverted in Grixis. The same energy is endlessly recycled and becomes more stagnant with each pass.
Sorin had created Avacyn, so it was a cruelty beyond imagining, a pain beyond description, that it fell upon him to end her forever.
He speaks directly into his supplicants' minds using fiery words that inflame their thoughts and incite their passions.
One offering to appease her on her arrival. Another to celebrate her departure.
Cinders carry an ancestral grudge that makes them slow to trust and quick to retaliate.
A power vacuum for the Azorius. A keepsake for Vraska.

"Finally, a weapon the Boros can't confiscate!"
—Juri, proprietor of the Juri Revue
Where Razia was aloof and untouchable, Aurelia is on the frontlines, calling for war.
Bant is a world where death and chaos hold no sway.
"The Sultai came hunting for a bear hide. Now I have a belt of naga skin, and my friend has a full belly."
It tears the flesh from your bones and then swallows the ash with its fiery maw.
The boar leads its rider to victory in battle, but it doesn't know how close it is to becoming the victory feast.
Those who regard the Gruul as savage simpletons underestimate the subtle power of their shamans.
By the law of church and crown, vampires feed only on the blood of the guilty—those declared heretics, rebels, or enemies of war.
"Your life serves a higher purpose now: ensuring the continuation of my own."
The progeny of the Maelstrom shows no allegiance—and no mercy—to any of the five shards.
She paints pictures with words, though not all pictures show the truth.
Snaking remnants of nature directed by a body of thought and progress, the oracles embody all that is Simic.
"I have faith in your potential."
Do not fear the lightning. Fear the one it obeys.
Elspeth's squires do not seek advancement. For them, no knightly glory could surpass the glory of serving their champion.
"Each year that passes rings you inwardly with memory and might. Wield your heart, and the world will tremble."
Dromoka's followers forsake blood ties so that they may join a greater family.
Silumgar never passes up an opportunity to add to his opulence.
Wracked and warped with anguish, it obsessively seeks out other souls to hoard within its eternal prison.
Her centuries-long search is ended.
Her wings are the prayers of the devoted; her sword, the despair of the vile.
If you want to wreak havoc above, sometimes it's best to look below.
When the rebels couldn't breach the castle to kill Lalor the Obstinate, they tried a more internal approach to depose the pretender king.
"Let's find out what kind of audience you are. Festive? Fearless?"
The peaks of Hurloon never fall silent.
Those who displease Oona soon learn the extent of the armies she commands.

"I am confident that if anyone actually penetrates our facades, even the most perceptive would still be fundamentally unprepared for the truth of House Dimir."
—Szadek

"This is a new world and a new war. We need warriors who know chaos and how to combat it."
—Lisha of the Azure
From death she grows living grandeur.
The Arbiter is a conduit of justice, a will so disciplined that it dispenses justice without ego or remorse.

"Taking down a dragon is easy. All you need is enough space to get in a good swing."
—Narbulg Nine Fingers

"The dragon has no pretense of compassion, no false mask of civilization—just hunger, heat, and need."
—Sarkhan Vol
Cries of anguish quickly spurred cries of action.
Havoc is a small price to pay for data.

"Chronicles across the ages describe Jodah. They likely refer not to one mage, but to a family or an arcane title."
—Arkol, Argivian scholar
At the end of the show, she stands alone on a stage brilliant with blood.
"I'll have my revenge if I have to call on every force from above and below."

"Rats and jackals feast in his swath, but even they will not walk with him."
—Mangara
He has "friends" in places both high and low, and all seem to owe him favors.
"Death tried to uncrown me. But now I return, king of a greater realm."
Alara's burning blood cannot be contained by mere earth and stone.

"Rage is not the answer. Rage followed by fitting vengeance is the answer."
—Ajani Goldmane
The forlorn cries of the dead combine to make its laugh.
He lurks in the undercity, eager for the corpse haulers to unload their rotting cargo.
"These benighted worlds are thick with ignorance. I will educate them. They will listen, or they will die."

"Yes, Boros tactics are unparalleled. But when your comrades are dying around you, inner strength must carry the day."
—Gideon Jura, to Aurelia
"Nature is a wonderful engineer but works far too slowly for my tastes."
"All will know of your crimes."
Olka collected the evening mist for years, studying its secrets. Once she learned its essence, she could vanish with a thought.

"My child grew from rot and ruin, yet she bloomed."
—Multani

"He is Yawgmoth's reward to me. I shall kill him a hundred times a day."
—Crovax, to Ertai

"We in the Conclave have a saying: 'When you hold a shield, lend your shield.' The strong must never forget what they owe to the weak."
—Niszka, Selesnya evangel

"Ludevic's laboratory is a veritable wonderland. I have never felt so inspired."
—Stitcher Geralf
"I turn around and see nothing, yet I know it is behind me. Its fingers rummage in my mind, crafting new ideas."
An elder in one pride, of the Sigiled caste in another.
Many sigils, one purpose.

"It's a cruel thing to give such a sad song to such a colorful creature."
—Sana, former Ahn-crop initiate
"Time and space are just new battlefields to be mastered."
For the Gruul, bone-crushing rage is the first priority. Accuracy comes in a distant ninetieth.
He bids his minions rise from their graves to their knees.
The vast network of predation on Jund has actually caused some strange creatures to adapt to being eaten.
The naga of the Sultai Brood made deals with dark forces to keep their power.
Leonos had no second thoughts about the abolishment edict. He'd left skyrunes warning of the eviction, even though it was cloudy.

"After death you face paradise, damnation, or Tariel."
—Priest's teaching

"The Tenth is under heavy attack, but it's being handled. I sent Mileva."
—Tajic
All suns must set.
The thoughtweft is his informant, and he its devoted guardian.
Ral's storm crackled with mystical detections: Planeswalkers were infiltrating Ravnica.
His name means "he who paints the earth red."

"Esper, like any work of art, can be truly appreciated only from a distance."
—Tezzeret
It strides through the whitecover, mists in which even gargantuans can hide.
Gold buys death. Death earns gold.
Once a fierce foe, she would become one of Madara's greatest protectors.
The nacatl called this new species "vetli," their word for poison arrows.
Zur remained aloof from Terisiare's suffering, intent only on his own perfection.
Spilled blood always begets more of the same.
Those without a guild signet often display a different form of protection.
The Phyrexian death machine awoke, its coldsteel heart imbuing it with sinister new power.
Amidst the darkest ashes grow the strongest seeds.

"If there can be no victory, then I will fight forever."
—Koth of the Hammer
In their hunger for the arch's power, mages often forget that it only makes dragons easier to summon. It doesn't make them easier to control.
The city mourned Niv-Mizzet's death, but he left behind the components for his rebirth.
All who listen hear their own song, a unique melody played just for them.

"Unskin these impure bodies, Great Yawgmoth, that the flesh may welcome your blessings."
—*Phyrexian Scriptures*
The fearful want the procedure before a blood festival. The guilty seek it afterward.

"It is finished. Now the real work can begin."
—Tezzeret

"What we call magic is nothing more than hope crystallized into a destination."
—Perisophia the philosopher
The model incorporated the fifth sun effortlessly, as if it had always known.

"There is much to learn here, but few can endure the ringing of the spires."
—Nulakam the Archivist
Built on the very ground where the Ten signed the Guildpact, the tower is a monument to the past and a reminder of who holds power in the present.
"Today's the last day you'll fear sewer crocs, Garg. From now on, the sewer crocs will fear you."
Ojutai sought to rewrite history. Those who disagreed sought the truth elsewhere.

"Oh, how I love gold. I'd eat and breathe it if I could."
—Leland, tax collector

"What will be has always been."
—Wall inscription
Blessed by the lands of winter.
Not even the most scathing critics can break her concentration.
"I suppose you've never heard of conservation of energy."
"If you make me spill my drink, you're buying me a new one."

"Sleep and dream, dream and snore,
While we fae complete our chore."
—Fae rhyme
From the veins of a peasant to the sketchbook of a master.
Their bodies rotted, their bones splintered, and their souls frayed to tatters. Only then were they granted the mercy of death.

"Oh, for heaven's sake, of course it was a death threat! What did you think was in an envelope like that, a wedding invitation?"
—Magistrate's assistant
You will scream out your innermost secrets just to make it stop.
Don't dig up the past if you're not prepared for the consequences.

"Toralf struck the ground with his hammer, and the force of a thousand storms tore through the demonic horde."
—Birgi, god of storytelling
Confused but undeterred, the butterflies charged into battle.
The fine print is illegible scribbles, but it *is* legally binding.

"My, how shocking."
—Barrin, Tolarian archmage

"No sign of movement. Looks like we've got the element of sur—"
—Gaiza, Mardu raider
"Why do they say you shouldn't play with fire? Fire is the best thing to play with!"
"What, these old things? They were just lying around, gathering dust. I figured I might as well put them to use."
